title: Fish fries, the red lantern and early jazz in New Orleans
summary: Roy Palmer played bass violin with a mandolin at the fish fries; a red lantern was the only advertisement, unlike the band parades for picnics.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, back to Roy Palmer and your fish fries. What instrument did he play at the fish fries? You said everything like that.
Bass violin, and he had a mandolin.
And what would they play, do you know?

Well, they was playing jazz music. Yeah, they was playing jazz music. I guess that's all they knew. That was the main thing. It's always been one of the main things in New Orleans, because there are other bands that play the quadrilles and things like that, you know. But that jazz music, ever since I've been knowing myself I've been hearing it. And so Roy was playing baritone, I saw him in a parade playing baritone and trombone.
Well, what went on at the fish fry? How did that work?
Well, she was selling fish. That's it. Selling fish.
How would the people know whether there was going to be a fish fry in the neighborhood?

Well, there would always be a lantern that would have a stick attached to the house. And on the very end, not too far so it would fall off, was this red lantern. So people would see that in the neighborhood and they knew that they would sell the fish. It was mostly on the side of this.
I often wondered how people would know about it. Yes. They didn't do any advertising for it.
Well, that was the advertisement, the red lantern.
I mean the band didn't go there.
No, no. That wasn't necessary. It wasn't like later on when they, like a picnic or a dancer would have these bands go around and advertise, mostly on a Sunday, you know.
